We rationed fresh water, mended torn canvas, and read aloud from worn novels to pass the hours. Storms south of the equator tested the rigging, with green waves breaking over the rail and men lashed to masts. Navigators argued over currents and winds, recalculating each noon from sun sights and dead reckoning. Supplies dwindled to hardtack and coffee, yet spirits lifted when lookouts spotted low hills on the horizon. Pilot boats guided us past reefs toward a sheltered bay lined with palms. Finally the logbook noted we anchored 12 nautical miles offshore.
